title: Where the Carryover Addition Enters a Standing Automatic Payment
content:
Where the carryover addition enters the settling of a fixed monthly sum on a card under Personal Credit Cards turns on the age of the card account and on recent card use.

*Where the card account has been open at least 48 whole months and card purchases posted to it in the last six months total at least 4000.00 USD* — the carryover addition is added to the product of the coverage share before the amount is spread over the statement cycles.

*Where the card account has been open at least 48 whole months and those purchases total less than 4000.00 USD* — the product of the coverage share is spread over the statement cycles first and the carryover addition is added to the spread figure afterwards.

*Where the card account has been open less than 48 whole months* — no carryover addition is made.

**Why the order matters.** On hypothetical figures of a product of the coverage share of 900.00 USD, a carryover addition of 45.00 USD and a spread over 3 statement cycles, the first convention spreads 945.00 USD and gives 315.00 USD a cycle, while the second spreads 900.00 USD to 300.00 USD and then adds 45.00 USD, giving 345.00 USD. The third gives 300.00 USD. The point at which the addition enters is therefore part of the rule.

**On the boundaries.** The age is read as at least, so an account open exactly 48 whole months takes one of the first two conventions and one open 47 whole months takes the third, whatever its purchases. The purchase figure separates at exactly 4000.00 USD, which belongs with the first convention.
